_doc: Enemy structures. The ask was 'add enemy structures like castles and forts and camps' and 'bandit camps … should have treasure chests to loot and bosses / quests tied to them'. So every entry here declares three things a player can take away — a named boss, a chest whose grade goes up with the tier, and a `gives` block of reward hooks — and `tests/poi.test.js` fails if any of them is missing. `plan` names a layout in data/setpieces.json; `on` says which world-map nodes it may sit on, which is what keeps a garrison at a pass or a junction instead of on a coordinate in an empty field. Original names only.

_schema.tier: 1 camp, 2 outpost, 3 fort, 4 castle — drives the chest grade, the garrison and how far off you can see it
_schema.on: world node types it may claim: landmark, pass, dungeon, crossing, road, junction. `road` and `junction` are worked out from world.roads, not from a node.
_schema.minBand: the lowest zone band that may hold one. A castle in the starting valley is not a landmark, it is a wall.
_schema.garrison: { count: [min,max], rankBonus, prefer: { roles, families } } — what js/sites.js asks the enemy field for
_schema.boss: { rank, modifiers, epithets } — every one of these gets a Name Forge given name and an epithet from this list
_schema.chest: { kind } — a key from balance.json's chests.kinds
_schema.gives: the reward hooks. At least one must be present or the POI test fails. R27: paid ONCE, when the boss goes down (js/sites.js `take`). `clears` = taking it clears the site for good (no garrison ever comes back; off, ordinary bodies may return but never a boss, prisoners or the strongbox). `opensDungeon` = an instance id from data/instances.json (or true for the vault) whose mouth opens within 40 m of the keep.
_schema.icon: 8.17 — the map glyph for this kind, so a fort and a lair are not the same dot. js/sites.js puts it on `site.pin.glyph`.

_chanceDoc: How often a slot of each type grows a garrison rather than a landmark. A road has three slots and a crossroads turns up every third shared cell, so those two have to stay low or the road becomes a gauntlet; a pass or a lair node is a place somebody would fortify, so those are close to even.

kinds.name: Bandit Camp
kinds.blurb: Tents round a fire behind a ring of stakes, and horses nobody paid for.

kinds.name: Raider Stockade
kinds.blurb: A stockade with two lookouts on it and cages inside the gate.

kinds.name: Held Watchtower
kinds.blurb: Somebody else's tower, with somebody else's flag on it.

kinds.name: Fort
kinds.blurb: A curtain of wall, four corner towers and a gate that is shut.

kinds.name: Castle
kinds.blurb: Two rings of wall, six towers and a keep you can see from the next valley.

kinds.name: Cult Circle
kinds.blurb: Nine stones, four fires and a slab that is wet in the middle of a dry season.

kinds.name: Beast Lair
kinds.blurb: A hole in a bank, a bone field around it, and a path worn flat by something heavy.

kinds.name: Siege Camp
kinds.blurb: Eight tents, three engines pointed the wrong way for you, and a town a mile off that has stopped opening its gate.

_r18Uses: R18 — the `uses` lists say which job frames a place can host, and were read by NOTHING; js/jobgen.js now prefers a frame a nearby landmark uses. Three of the eleven ids named no frame at all: `burn_it_out` -> push_them_out, `cull` -> thin_the_pack, and `hold_the_line`, which is a MERCENARY ABILITY id from data/mercenaries.json rather than a frame -> the_claim. A guard test now fails on any `uses` id that is not a real frame, so the join cannot dangle again.
